input.d8_retired_2026_08_21: The d8 half graded support-matrix D8 while D8 was an OPEN wall-clock breach: it recomputed the published range from the reports the row cited and required the row to cite them. M12 (PR #20, ADR-013) then CLOSED D8 — the row no longer publishes a breach range, so there is nothing left for this half to recompute, and it was failing on a row that had legitimately changed rather than on a defect. Retired rather than re-pointed because the number it protected is now gated directly and better: `fast-wall-clock-budget` asserts the suite's own wall clock against the ceiling (60s local, 80s CI) and `wall-clock-probe-history-isolated` covers the history side, so a regression reddens the gate itself instead of a prose range. The reports it cited (20260821-215759/215923-fast.json) were measured pre-M12 and are now uncited; they are prune candidates under ADR-012. The README-counts half stays — nothing else derives those, and it reddens the moment a case is added.

triage.note: tagged invariant — a hand-maintained count is wrong again by the next milestone, and this repo has already burned a review round on three documents carrying three different totals for the same thing (PR #15, R19). The failure mode this closes is not the wrong number, it is the number that nothing recomputes. Adding a case to the suite now turns this red until README is updated, which is the intended cost. D8's cited reports are immutable artifacts, so its assertion is stable; moving the range means citing the runs it was measured from. The block cites report files rather than recomputing 'the latest run' on purpose: a report is immutable, so the assertion is stable, and moving the block means citing the runs it was measured from — the same contract D8's retired half had.
